IS THE LOOP LEARNING OR REPEATING? Learning, but the last two entries are a groove. #214 and #215 are the fifth and sixth SALT in this town (WIND_SALT, the cart, the fair, freeBay, RIVER_SALT), the law for the move was already written before either ran, and both shipped under 35 lines. That is a MENU problem, not a town problem, and the answer is to climb rather than to run it a seventh time.

WHAT I KILLED BEFORE WRITING IT. The pass from #210 named Interaction as the next climb — 15 of 210 iterations, 8 of them sill chrome, four domains at zero. I priced that on HEAD and it is wrong. courtyard.html's click handler already answers BED/CBED (you scatter seed), GRASS (a daisy), REED, ICE, SHOAL, WATER (the ducks come), and SIDE/ROAD/PATH (crumbs, and three birds land); lookAt names every drawn thing under the pointer; a tap on a person follows them; OFFERS is a five-deep invitation queue that spends each offer whether it is spoken or not. The 'four domains at zero' figure is a COVERAGE-GRID ARTIFACT: interaction in this town is written by TILE, not by domain, so it never lands in a domain's row. The grid was measuring its own bookkeeping.

WHERE THE FRONTIER ACTUALLY IS. The town's VOCABULARY has stopped growing. The runlog's scalars are ladder SUMS over census.mjs's nine runs, so speciesKinds 117 is 9 x SPECIES.length — and SPECIES has stood at 13 since #155, SIXTY iterations. tileKinds 174 has not moved since #192, when SHOAL made it 21 kinds. The town is getting more of what it already has. mapFlat does not fire because its definition ORs tileKinds with structures and structures is alive — so I am naming the flat half before the signal will, exactly as the #210 pass named the diff flattening before smallDiff did.

RUNG 4b, AND THE LADDER DID NOT FORCE IT. The rule allows a second consecutive pass at rung <= 2 and I am declining it; the census is the reason, not the counter. Last 4b was the pass from #185 — since then 5, 4a, 3, 5, 2. b216 is a SPATIAL change to the largest region in the world and is the only brief here that can move tileKinds.

queue.brief: Three quantized triggers dirty the same ground cache and they disagree about the rule. weedBucket() repaints on ANY change over 102 cells; snow holds a deadband of 3% (SNOW_REPAINT); ice, added at #210, holds 8 of 2860 (ICE_REPAINT). One of the three is priced wrong and nobody has ever compared them. The law is already written for this: before adding a trigger, price what ALREADY dirties that cache — the incumbent's rate caps the new one's mean win — so buy the WORST CASE and set the deadband where the PICTURE stops, not where the count does. Make it one rule, in the weather each trigger actually owns: a thaw, a snowfall, a rank August.
queue.successLooksLike: One stated rule covers all three, with the repaint RATE and drawGround's cost quoted before and after in each trigger's own weather, and a shown threshold at which the difference image stops changing.
queue.avoid: The incumbent caps the win: if lightMoved/LIGHT_MOVE already dirties the cache more often than all three put together, say so with the number — 'no change is warranted' is a finding and this brief accepts it, provided the number is there. Read the REPORTER, not the producer: perf.mjs is vsync-locked, so time drawGround as a function, in its weather, at every camera. And a threshold is priced off the subject's FASTEST phase, never its mean.

The cross street is laid to the same standard (roadway XS_R0 68..XS_R1 74 in setts via settGrid/settRun, two footways, kerbs, lamps, TREE_PITS) and in 215 iterations nothing has ever driven it. The two roads meet at the lane's north kerb, in the middle of the wide frame, and the junction is not a junction — it is two stripes that cross. Make them one network.

queue.successLooksLike: Watch the junction for a minute of a busy hour and something turns out of the lane into the cross street, or down out of it — and the turn is legible: the rig slows, something behind it holds, the heading swings. Quoted as turns per market morning against a control, not as a single screenshot.
queue.avoid: Do not add a fifth vehicle kind — there are four and the census says they are not under-used. drawRig already draws from t.hx/t.hy, so the heading is a vector: TURN the heading rather than special-casing a sprite. A turning rig crosses a footway, so price it against the walking lines (LANE_N_Y/LANE_S_Y, XS_WALK_W/E) and against the keep-left convention it is leaving. Traffic runs off hash(simT), never R() — keep it that way or the whole seeded world reshuffles.

queue.brief: The census is issuing FAILs that are its own sampling, and the saturation note on this cell asks for exactly that: a gate that FAILED. #214 shipped over census FAIL winter/frozen 1063 -> 1030, -3.1% against a 3% floor, on a change that was a pure redistribution — and FOUR HEAD-only, behaviour-free re-keyings of freeBay put frozen at 1059/1054/1032/1041. The floor is inside the noise of a reshuffle that means nothing. c309 adds the mechanism: WCORE's winter cell (warp 1220) is sampled MID-FREEZE, on the ramp, so a 1.7% move in an unrelated constant took it to 956 (probes/winter-drift.mjs). c313 is the same disease in another field: census martinNests read +46 (130 -> 176) on a change probes/mart-clock.mjs put at +2.1 on +-7.9 over 24 seed-years — nine pinned instants cannot weigh a threshold CA.
queue.successLooksLike: The winter cell is sampled somewhere its own value is not sprinting — a plateau, not the ramp — or its floor is set off the MEASURED noise of a behaviour-free re-keying, with the number quoted and the choice argued; and every field the nine-instant ladder cannot resolve (martinNests first) either gets a wider sample or is marked as unresolvable so a worker does not chase it. Re-run every gate that reads the subject you redefine, and pin the before to a REF.
queue.avoid: Do not loosen the floor until the FAILs stop — a gate that cannot fail is not a gate. Measure the noise by re-keying the CANDIDATE, not HEAD, and set the bound off that measurement. Harness costs a domain nothing and is expected to log srcChanged:false; it must still change a NUMBER somebody reads.
